topic: Ordowski's least prime offsets and a Fermat-number covering
title: Exact Fermat-divisor formulas for Ordowski's prime-offset conjecture, extending Crocker's covering method

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Crocker's Fermat-number covering argument (1971, Lemma I, p. 104), we prove the conjecture posed by Thomas Ordowski in the first COMMENTS line of OEIS A369378, revision 40 (13 February 2024): 2^(2^n+1)-1+2^k is not prime when n>0 and 0<=k<2^n. The divisor is the Fermat number indexed by the exponent of 2 in k>0; the case k=0 is a power of 2. An exact greatest-common-divisor identity extends the obstruction to every positive k not divisible by 2^n and gives the corresponding restriction for absolute differences from 2^(2^n-1)-1. The latter recovers a special case of Crocker's 1971 Lemma I and isolates the residue class not covered in Ordowski's related absolute-difference conjecture. The arguments do not require Fermat numbers to be prime.
summary: For n>=1, every positive prime offset is divisible by 2^n. Exact gcd identities describe the Fermat-number obstruction for both sums and absolute differences; the full related absolute-difference conjecture remains outside this coverage.
